messages:
mike: Heads up — since the driver 504 rollout to us-west-2 nodes we've seen a spike in failed NVLink P2P handshakes on several A100 pools. Instances are falling back to PCIe and throughput drops ~3-4x.
anya: seeing the same in our dashboard (us-west-2-gpu-*). Latency SLOs are breaching on batching jobs.
devops-bot: [ALERT] 504-driver-upgrade: 18 hosts reporting 'p2p_disabled' kernel messages — rate 22/min — triggered at 2026-03-18T14:05:23Z :warning:
linda: Can you paste the kernel message snippet, @mike? Wondering if it's BAR1 related or ACS config getting flipped.
mike: log tail from one affected host below:
```
Mar 18 13:59:02 compute-a100-12 kernel: p2p: nvlink handshake failed, PEER_ACCESS_DENIED
Mar 18 13:59:02 compute-a100-12 kernel: pci 0000:03:00.0: BAR1 window: requested 0x20000000, assigned 0x10000000
Mar 18 13:59:02 compute-a100-12 nvidia: p2p: disabled due to BAR1 window shrinkage
```
rafa: that BAR1 assignment looks smaller than our spec. Could be driver requesting different aperture after kmod change. We saw similar with 495->500, but not this magnitude. Any kernel ABI changes in 5.10->5.15 can affect ACS/PCIe resource accounting.
anya: cluster-autoscaler noted increased pending pods because these nodes couldn't hit the batching throughput. Cost projection for next 24h if fallbacks continue = +$8.2k (extra instances + longer job runtime).
linda: status of canary? Which shard got 504 first?
mike: rollout staged to canary pool in us-west-2 (10 hosts) ~10:30 UTC, then to rest at 11:50 UTC. Canary had 2/10 failures but we missed early alarms.
infra-runner: quick grep across fleet shows pattern: failures concentrated on hosts with PCIe rootport firmware v1.3.1 and kernel 5.15.0-48. Hosts with rootport v1.2.x and kernel 5.10 are mostly fine.
rafa: that points to interplay between driver 504's BAR1 negotiation and newer rootport firmware resource clamp. Suggest reverting driver on affected hosts and re-run p2p selftest.
anya: agree. Recommend targeted rollback for us-west-2 and pause rollout elsewhere. Also open support ticket w/ vendor for firmware+driver compatibility.
devops-bot: [ACTION] rollback-driver 504 -> 500 scheduled for us-west-2-group-a at 15:00 UTC (manual confirm required).
mike: I'll hold the rollback until we confirm safe window. Can infra team collect a KV cache dump and dmesg from 3 example hosts? Need to see if caching layers are impacted.
linda: collecting now. attaching brief telemetry (top lines):
```
host compute-a100-12: nvlink_rx_err_rate=0.08, p2p_disabled=1, throughput_gpu=2100 tokens/s (baseline 8800)
host compute-a100-23: nvlink_rx_err_rate=0.00, p2p_disabled=0, throughput_gpu=9000 tokens/s
```
mike: thanks. Two notes: 1) NCCL reports increased falls back to ring/PCIe which increases cross-host traffic. 2) This will hammer network links and make autoscaler spin up more nodes.
rafa: if rollback not feasible fast, we can patch runtime to prefer older fallback routing (keep local on-die caching) and throttle batch size to avoid triggering NVLink handshake. Might save cost short-term.
anya: ok let's do triage plan: 1) pause global rollout, 2) rollback driver on affected pool, 3) collect vendor logs and open ticket, 4) add temporary runtime throttles and smaller batch suggestion in Canary config.
mike: I'm authorizing rollback. @devops-bot kick it off and ensure drain isn't aggressive (we want in-place driver swap with minimal pod churn).
devops-bot: rollback job started. will update status in thread. :gear:
infra-runner: dmesg and nvlink diagnostics uploaded to /internal/infra/telemetry/1855012345/ — grep 'BAR1' and 'p2p' for quick markers.
linda: one more data point — us-east-1 didn't get the 504 rollout yet; ramps there should be paused until we confirm resolution.
rafa: also cc'ing firmware team — if rootport firmware needs patching, we should coordinate a combined driver+fw test matrix.
mike: agreed. Post-rollback we'll run a canary with expanded telemetry (nvlink errors, BAR1 window size, NCCL ring fallback count).
anya: noted for cost ops — estimate rollback + slower throughput penalties = ~$2.1k for the next 24h but avoids the larger +$8k hit.
mike: thanks all. updates as they happen. :thumbsup:
